messages:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT PAGE — HIGH 5xx RATE on gateway-prod :rotating_light:
incident-bot: Pager: gateway-prod (severity: P1) — spike in TLS handshake failures and 502/504s, paging oncall Maya.
oncall-bot: Escalation policy: primary oncall Maya, fallback Rafa.
Maya: I'm on it. seeing a large spike in client TLS handshake failures hitting gateway-prod-edge. Starting triage.
Maya: quick check — any recent cert rotations? @rafa
Rafa: Not from infra, scheduled rotator ran last night but I don't see obvious errors in rotator logs. Pulling logs now.
Maya: Checking Grafana — TLS handshake failures correlate with increased 502/504s from gateway frontends to origin pools. Errors show "tlsv1 alert unknown ca" and "SSL routines:tls_construct_client_hello:wrong version number" in proxy logs.
Samira: Could this be an expired intermediate? We had a CA chain rotation last month.
Cheng: Checking CA expiry: root and leaf look fine in cert DB. Intermediate cert (CA-2024-interm) expired 10:02 UTC. That matches spike.
Alex: Confirmed from cert-monitor: CA-2024-interm expired at 10:02 UTC — some mTLS clients reject chain now, others fall back but hit 502s.
Maya: Customer impact: routing errors for ~12% of traffic to EU/US gateways, some requests hitting Dedicated instances. Paging customers? ops-sla? @alex
Alex: We'll prepare status: impact ~10-15% of requests, increased latency and 5xx rates. No data exposure.
Maya: Mitigation plan: 1) Short-term: enable permissive chain acceptance on edge (allow alternative chain / accept leaf-only) 2) Re-issue and push new intermediate ASAP 3) Update rotator to catch expiry alerts earlier.
Rafa: I can push permissive mode on gateway-proxies to accept chain without intermediate for up to 30 minutes. Rolling change to EU first. Command: ``sudo /usr/local/bin/gwctl set tls.accept_loose_chain=true --env=prod --region=eu``
Maya: Do it. Notify when done.
Rafa: Rolling to EU now — 3/3 pods updated. Monitoring.
Maya: Telemetry — TLS handshake failures drop by ~60% in EU after permissive toggle. US still high. Rolling to US now.
Rafa: US roll started. 5/5 pods.
Maya: US drop looks similar. Overall 5xx down to baseline-ish but still elevated for some clients that enforce strict mTLS validation.
Cheng: For strict clients we need a reissued intermediate chain. I'm generating CSR to intermediary CA now.
Cheng: New intermediate signed — uploading to rotator. Pushing new chain to rotator service: ``POST /rotator/v1/push-chain -d '{"cert_id":"ca-2026-interm","pem":"-----BEGIN CERT..."}'``
Samira: Rotator accepted chain, starting rollout to edge proxies and dedicated pools. ETA ~8 minutes.
Maya: While rotator rolls, add temporary fallback: route traffic from specific IP ranges to fallback cluster without strict mTLS check. Use route-tag env: ``/routing/override?tag=perm-fallback``
Alex: Routing change applied for top 5 customer IP ranges. Monitoring customer error rates.
Maya: Rotator reports 100% rollout in EU/US. New intermediate in place.
Cheng: Validations: I queried client handshakes — clients now see full chain and mTLS handshakes complete. OCSP stapling present.
Maya: Confirming error rates returning to normal. Closing pager in 30m after stability window.
Rafa: Postmortem notes: rotator missed expiry alert for intermediate; metrics alert threshold too coarse. We'll add 14-day and 48-hour expiry alerts, and a synthetic mTLS handshake check across regions every 6 hours.
Samira: Action items assigned: Rafa (rotator alert thresholds + runbook updates), Cheng (rotate and automate intermediate renewals), Maya (customer comms & postmortem).
Alex: Drafting status update for customers. Will post on status.redwoodinfra.com: "Partial gateway errors due to expired intermediate CA — mitigated, services restored"
Maya: Thanks team. Will follow up with full postmortem. :white_check_mark:
oncall-bot: Incident resolved for now — monitoring continues.
incident-bot: Summary: root cause: expired intermediate CA leading to mTLS handshake failures; mitigations: permissive chain acceptance, routing fallbacks, reissued intermediate and rotator rollout; impact: ~10-15% of requests experienced increased 5xx/timeouts; no data loss.
